[[File:Jiří Welsch in 2005.jpg|thumb|275px|Welsch (right) with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in 2005]]
'''Jiří Welsch''' ({{IPA|cs|ˈjɪr̝iː ˈvɛlʃ}}) (born 27 January 1980) is a Czech former professional [[basketball]] player who played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) from 2002 to 2006 with the [[Golden State Warriors]], [[Boston Celtics]], [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], and [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. He was selected by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the first round of the [[2002 NBA draft]].

==Professional career==

===Early years===
Welsch began his professional career as a teenager with [[BK JIP Pardubice]] of the [[National Basketball League (Czech Republic)|Czech Republic League]], where he played until 1998. He then signed with [[BC Sparta Prague|CSA Sparta Prague]] of the Czech Republic League for the 1998–99 season, and then he moved to [[KK Olimpija|Union Olimpija Ljubljana]] of the [[Premier A Slovenian Basketball League|Slovenian League]], where he played until 2002. He was named the Slovenian League [[Most Valuable Player]] following the 2001–02 season campaign.

===NBA===
Welsch was drafted by the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]'s [[Philadelphia 76ers]] with the 16th selection of the [[2002 NBA draft]], but he was immediately traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]] for a future first-round draft pick and a future first- or second-round draft pick.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nbadraft/story?id=1399443 The wheeling and dealing on draft night]</ref> He spent one season with the Warriors, averaging 1.6 points per game, 0.8 rebounds per game, and 0.7 assists per game in 37 games in the [[2002–03 NBA season|2002–03 season]] before he was traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]], along with [[Antawn Jamison]], [[Chris Mills (basketball)|Chris Mills]] and [[Danny Fortson]], in exchange for [[Evan Eschmeyer]], [[Nick Van Exel]], [[Avery Johnson]], [[Popeye Jones]] and [[Antoine Rigaudeau]] on 18 August 2003.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=1598671 Mavs send Van Exel, four others to Warriors]</ref> Without ever playing a game for them, Welsch, along with Mills, [[Raef LaFrentz]] and a lottery-protected [[2004 NBA draft]] pick, was traded by Dallas to the [[Boston Celtics]] on 20 October 2003 in exchange for [[Antoine Walker]] and [[Tony Delk]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/espnmag/story?section=magazine&id=3756860 Seems like a miracle, but somehow Antoine Walker is back where he belongs.], by Tom Friend</ref> Welsch started 68 games for the Celtics in the [[2003–04 NBA season|2003–04 season]], averaging 9.2 points per game.<ref name=malaga/>

Welsch averaged 8.5 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 2.0 assists per game in 136 games played (100 of them starts) in 2003–04 and [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05]], while playing with the Celtics. On 24 February 2005, Welsch was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] for a future [[2007 NBA draft|2007 first-round draft pick]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=1998808 Cavs acquire Welsch for '07 first-round pick]</ref>

On 28 June 2005, Welsch was traded by the Cavs to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for a [[2006 NBA draft|2006 second-round draft pick]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2005/news/story?id=2096451 Cavs receive 2006 second-round pick]</ref>

Welsch's final NBA game was played in Game 5 of the 2006 Eastern Conference First Round on 3 May 2006, against the [[Detroit Pistons]]. The Bucks would lose the game 93–122 and drop the series to Detroit 4–1, with Welsch recording 2 points, 1 assist and 1 rebound.

===Back to Europe===
In August 2006, Welsch decided to leave the NBA, and he signed with the Spanish [[Liga ACB|ACB league]] club [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja Málaga]].<ref name=malaga>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2542747 Bucks' Welsch signs with Malaga in Spain]</ref> After playing with [[CB Estudiantes|Estudiantes Madrid]], he signed a contract with [[Spirou Basket]], of [[Belgium]], in July 2011.<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/belgium/28484/spirou_charleroi_tabs_jiri_welsch.html Spirou Charleroi tabs Jiri Welsch]</ref> In 2012, he signed with [[Basketball Nymburk|ČEZ Nymburk]].<ref>[http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2012-13/i/101295/7363/cez-nymburk-brings-czech-star-welsch-home CEZ NYMBURK brings Czech star Welsch home] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130214152702/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2012-13/i/101295/7363/cez-nymburk-brings-czech-star-welsch-home |date=14 February 2013 }}</ref> He joined BK Pardubice in 2017.

==National team career==
Welsch has been a member of the senior [[Czech Republic national basketball team]]. He played at the following [[EuroBasket]] tournaments: the [[1999 EuroBasket]], the [[2007 EuroBasket]], the [[2013 EuroBasket]], the [[2015 EuroBasket]], and the [[2017 EuroBasket]].
